component.name: Accordion
component.description: A vertical list of collapsible sections (Accordion.Item). Each section has a header button with a title, an optional subtitle and a chevron, inside a heading of the page's outline (h3 by default, headingLevel on the root). Activating the header shows or hides the section's content. Sections open independently — several can be open at once — and each is uncontrolled (defaultOpen) or controlled (open + onOpenChange). Used for course curricula and FAQs.

when: Listing course modules where each can be expanded to read its description
An FAQ where each question reveals its answer
Pass subtitle for a secondary line under the title (e.g. a module's duration '4 hours, 30min')
Set headingLevel on Accordion so section titles sit one level below the surrounding section heading (default 3, under an h2 section)
Use defaultOpen for a section that starts open; use open + onOpenChange when the app needs to drive or track the open state

patterns.name: course-curriculum
patterns.description: A course page's curriculum: one item per module, subtitle carries the module duration, content is the module description. Story: Default.

patterns.name: faq
patterns.description: Question/answer list without subtitles. Story: WithoutSubtitle.

patterns.name: controlled-sections
patterns.description: The app owns which sections are open (e.g. persisted progress). Story: Controlled.

antiPatterns.reason: The item reads headingLevel from the root's context and throws without it.

antiPatterns.scenario: Passing a heading, button or link as the title, or putting interactive controls in the subtitle
antiPatterns.reason: The title and subtitle render inside the header <button>; nested interactive or heading content is invalid and breaks the button's accessible name.
antiPatterns.alternative: Pass plain strings to title and subtitle; put links and actions in the item's children.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using Accordion for navigation or for a single show/hide toggle elsewhere on the page
antiPatterns.reason: Accordion is a list of headed sections that belong to the page outline.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use TextLink/nav for navigation; use a transparent Button with aria-expanded for a one-off toggle.

antiPatterns.scenario: Setting headingLevel that skips levels in the outline (e.g. h5 directly under an h2 section)
antiPatterns.reason: Section titles are real headings; skipped levels confuse screen-reader heading navigation.
antiPatterns.alternative: Set headingLevel to one below the nearest enclosing heading.

purpose.false: Closed Accordion.Item: header only, chevron-down, content hidden. Uncontrolled default (defaultOpen=false).
purpose.true: Open Accordion.Item: elevated background, chevron-up, content shown under the subtitle. Set via defaultOpen, or controlled via open + onOpenChange. Independent per item — several can be open at once.

states.description: Header only; chevron-down; content hidden (hidden attribute). Story: AllClosed.
Elevated container background; chevron-up; content shown under the subtitle. Story: Default (second item).
subtitle omitted — header shows the title only. Story: WithoutSubtitle.

ariaAttributes: Header <button> inside an h{headingLevel} (default h3) — WAI-ARIA APG accordion pattern
aria-expanded on the header button reflects whether the section is open
aria-controls on the header button → the panel id
aria-labelledby on the header button → the title, so the heading and button are named by the title alone; aria-describedby → the subtitle when present
Panel: role=region, aria-labelledby → the title (same id the header button uses); hidden attribute when closed

keyboardInteractions.action: Moves focus between section headers and any focusable content in open panels
Toggles the focused section open or closed
Moves focus to the next / previous section header, wrapping at the ends
Moves focus to the first / last section header

parts.name: Item
parts.description: One collapsible section. Props: title (string), subtitle (string, optional), open, defaultOpen (false), onOpenChange, and children — the section content shown in the panel (free-form; accepts lists the expected components). Layout of header, subtitle, chevron and panel is owned by Accordion.module.css. Accordion itself is the context provider (no separate Accordion.Root): it has no preset content props to rebuild from parts, so the guard reads 'Accordion.Item must be rendered inside Accordion'.
